constitutive_assumptions: The self-weight of the particles within the passive chamber is negligible.
Particles are spherical with diameter D and arrange such that each particle is surrounded by six neighboring particles.
Particle squeezing occurs under external relative pressure P with an effective particle contact area assumed to be A = pi*D^2 / 4, yielding an interaction force F = pi*D^2*P / 4.
Friction between contacting particles follows Coulomb friction with a constant friction coefficient mu_f, where normal force FN = sqrt(3)*FP / 3.
Displacement of each particle layer across the particle pack is uniform (1dF = D*dF / h), where h is the total pack height and m = h / D is the number of layers.
Equivalent resultant friction force fR from particle jamming acts at the geometric midpoint of the actuator (resultant friction force arm lf = lF / 2).
Finger arc segments AB, CD, and EF maintain constant arc lengths during bending, while intermediate segments MA, BC, DE, and NF remain completely straight.
Bending angle of the entire finger divides equally among the three active bending arcs (phi / 3 per arc).
Actuation bending torque generated by internal pressure against the distal chamber end follows the relationship MP = a^2 * w * P / 2.
control_variables: Palm actuation air pressure (maintained constant at 200 kPa during holding tests)
Linear guide displacement distance (d = 5 mm during finger rotational stiffness tests)
Finger cross-sectional dimensions (air chamber height a = 15 mm, width w = 16 mm, particle chamber depth d = 10 mm, particle diameter D = 3 mm)
Sensor circuit input reference voltage (5 V)
Ambient testing conditions and camera setup distance
dependent_variables: Rotational stiffness of the finger (k, N*mm/rad)
Radius of curvature of the bending finger (rho, mm)
Electrical resistance change of conductive TPU feedback modules (Delta R, ohms)
Maximum holding weight / load capacity before grasp failure (kg)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Passive granular jamming induced by pressurized pneumatic actuation increases the rotational stiffness of the soft finger by 2.14 times (from 1223 N*mm/rad to 2621 N*mm/rad) at 450 kPa without requiring a dedicated vacuum source.

Enclosing loose granular particles in the passive chamber increases the bending radius of curvature at lower pressures, but this discrepancy diminishes and becomes practically negligible at operating pressures around 400 to 450 kPa.
A five-fingered soft robotic hand with particle-filled passive chambers achieved a maximum holding capacity of 1.452 kg compared to 0.8425 kg without particles at an actuation pressure of 450 kPa.
An analytical rotational stiffness model combining air pressure torque and particle friction work accurately captures the experimental stiffness progression across increasing actuation pressures.

Multi-material fused deposition modeling (FDM) enables single-process automatic additive fabrication of soft pneumatic elastomeric chambers and integrated conductive TPU piezoresistive position feedback sensors.

Piezoresistive conductive TPU sensors embedded at finger joints demonstrate quadratic calibration relationships between resistance change and joint bending angles, allowing reconstruction of fingertip positions.
Integrating an independently actuated soft palm capable of metacarpal bending and secondary bending facilitates effective grasping of geometrically diverse everyday objects.

experimental_setup: Hand motion test: Evaluation of five fingers and palm actuation using pressure control valves (SMC AR20-01-A) at 400 kPa for fingers and 200 kPa for the palm, recorded via palmar and top camera views.

Finger rotational stiffness test: Ring finger actuated from 0 to 450 kPa in 50 kPa increments via an electro-pneumatic regulator (SMC ITV2030-212L); a stepper motor-driven linear guide pushed the finger 5 mm against a 0-100 N digital force meter (0.01 N precision), with 10 repeated measurements per pressure level.
Finger curvature test: HD video camera recording the radius of curvature of the bending finger across pressures from 0 to 450 kPa with and without embedded particles.

Position feedback calibration and tracking: Index finger joints marked and tracked with an HD camera while resistance changes were measured using digital multimeters (Victor 86D); position tracing evaluated across 0 to 400 kPa in 80 kPa steps via an Arduino Nano and a 24-bit ADS1256 ADC circuit with standard reference resistors.

Hand holding test: Horizontally oriented hand gripping a custom 3D printed test part with raised features under 200 kPa palm pressure and 325 to 450 kPa finger pressure (25 kPa steps), with suspended weights added until grasp failure over 5 repeated trials per condition.
Object grasping demonstration: Grasping 11 diverse everyday items (baseball, orange, box, metal bottle, wallet, cellphone, egg carton, loudspeaker, tape roll, multimeter, champagne bottle).
future_work: Integrating position feedback sensing modules into all five fingers and the palm.
Implementing closed-loop position and trajectory control and developing sophisticated grasping strategies based on sensor feedback.
Integrating tactile sensors into the hand to provide more accurate touch and contact feedback.
Further investigating theoretical models of the passive jamming phenomenon to optimize structural hand performance.
independent_variables: Granular particle inclusion state (passive chamber filled with particles vs. empty)
Joint bending angle / lateral deflection displacement
limitations_inferred: Stiffness variation is strictly coupled to the pneumatic actuation pressure, preventing independent control of joint stiffness and bending deflection.
Long-term electrical hysteresis, drift, and cyclic degradation of the 3D-printed conductive TPU piezoresistive sensors were not characterized.
Mechanical fatigue, wear, and airtightness durability of the FDM-printed NinjaFlex chambers subjected to repeated pressurization and particle contact friction were not evaluated.

Holding performance verification relied on an object specifically designed with raised surface features to enhance interlocking, which may not reflect grasping performance on smooth or low-friction surfaces.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Position feedback modules were only fabricated and evaluated on the index finger rather than all five fingers and palm.
Discrepancies between analytical stiffness predictions and experimental measurements arose from test errors and simplified modeling assumptions.
Deviations between visual ground truth and sensor-derived fingertip position tracking were caused by environmental disturbances and calibration inaccuracies.
Carbon black particles in the conductive TPU filament tend to clog FDM printer nozzles over extended printing periods, requiring nozzle cleaning with PLA.
Particles must be loaded manually into the passive chamber post-printing through a slot and sealed with hot melt adhesive.
Holding tests could not be performed below 325 kPa finger pressure because the finger bending curvature was insufficient to secure the grasped test object.
main_results: The soft finger achieved a rotational stiffness of 2621 N*mm/rad with particles compared to 1223 N*mm/rad without particles at 450 kPa, representing a 2.14-fold stiffness increase.
The soft robotic hand with particle-filled fingers achieved a maximum holding load of 1.452 kg compared to 0.8425 kg without particles at 450 kPa actuation pressure.
Finger bending radius of curvature differences between particle-filled and empty chambers decreased with increasing pressure, becoming negligible around 400 kPa.
Analytical predictions of finger rotational stiffness closely matched the experimental trends across actuation pressures from 0 to 450 kPa.
Piezoresistive sensor calibration curves fitted with quadratic polynomials enabled fingertip position estimation consistent with visual camera measurements.
The bio-inspired soft hand demonstrated successful dexterous grasping across 11 objects of varying shape, size, and weight.
modeling_methods: Analytical rotational stiffness modeling combining moment equilibrium, geometrical kinematic relations of segmented arc bending, internal pneumatic pressure torque, and Coulomb friction work among jammed spherical particles.
Kinematic forward modeling of the three-joint finger based on rigid-link geometric transformations to estimate fingertip coordinates from individual joint angles.
Empirical polynomial regression (quadratic curve fitting) relating conductive TPU electrical resistance variations to joint bending rotation angles.
performance_metrics: Sensor electrical resistance change (Delta R, ohms)
Fingertip tracking position coordinates (x, y, mm)
possible_gap_implications: Developing mechanisms that decouple variable stiffness from bending actuation to allow stiffness modulation at arbitrary finger postures.
Investigating fully automated manufacturing workflows capable of directly incorporating granular jamming media without manual filling and adhesive sealing steps.
Developing dynamic compensation and filtering algorithms to address piezoresistive sensor drift and hysteresis in additive soft robotics.
paper.research_objective: To design, model, automatically fabricate using multi-material 3D printing, and experimentally evaluate a bio-inspired soft smart robotic hand featuring independent palm actuation, passive granular jamming for actuation-coupled stiffening without vacuum pumps, and embedded conductive elastomer sensors for joint position feedback.
paper.research_problem: Conventional soft material robots lack sufficient force output and load-holding capacity due to the low rigidity of soft materials, commonly lack integrated position sensing that preserves compliance, typically rely on heavy and cumbersome vacuum equipment for granular jamming, and frequently neglect active palm actuation in hand designs.
paper.title: Design and Automatic Fabrication of Novel Bio-Inspired Soft Smart Robotic Hands
